correctness.rationale: For n>=4, the three nonzero Laplacian eigenvalue classes are A=2w+(n-2)x, D=2x+(n-2)y (multiplicity n-3), and nx. Their inverse sum is the exact Kirchhoff index divided by n. Strict convexity and price-preserving automorphisms force the unique global minimizer into these classes. Cauchy–Schwarz with the exact transformed budget produces the claimed cheap-edge equality case; the two positivity inequalities show feasibility exactly through tau=n/(n-2). On the w=0 face a second sharp Cauchy–Schwarz inequality gives the plateau solution. Repricing-and-rescaling rules out w>0 at higher prices. S and its first two derivatives verify the quadratic contact. The packaged full-Laplacian and exact symbolic tests passed; their finite range is not substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Dense redundant networks with nonuniform link costs lead to a natural and decision-relevant question: at which price can a direct edge optimally be eliminated if every remaining conductance is reoptimized? The unique complete-graph solution answers it at the sharp threshold 1+2/(n-2), proves all other edges remain positive, gives a closed-form design/value, and exhibits quadratic contact and an O(1/n) critical price premium. This is a genuine infinite-family structural support change, not a mere numerical example or relabeling of the known equal-price clique.
